task.name: A broken-baseline abort discards the gate's failure evidence and deletes the worktree that produced it
task.story_text:
## What happened

Sprint run `9c81cc51af26` (`issues-1415,2154,2155,2150`, base `release/v0.13`,
2026-08-03) aborted before dispatching any story:

```
RuntimeError: Broken baseline: configured gate failed on sprint merge base
d8fcf7b464faf2e3240e422ed8b870c82d062bef before any dev work started (Gate returned FAIL)
```

The gate result was `1 failed, 6865 passed, 32 skipped, 13 warnings in 61.87s`.
The whole sprint was halted by that one failure, at a reported cost of $0.00,
with all four stories left in `waiting`.

Two artifacts needed to establish whether the baseline was genuinely broken were
gone by the time the abort was investigated, minutes later:

- The run log retained only the pytest summary line naming the failing test
  (`FAILED tests/test_process_group.py::TestGroupMembers::test_lists_every_live_process_in_the_group`).
  Grepping the log for an assertion, traceback, captured stdout or error text for
  that test returns nothing. The one-line summary is the entire record.
- The worktree the gate ran in, `.forge/forge-baseline-hdkth9k6/worktree`, no
  longer existed, so the failure could not be re-run in the environment that
  produced it.

`d8fcf7b` is the checkout's HEAD. Running the named test against that same commit
outside the gate passes 34 of 34, three consecutive times. The failure therefore
does not reproduce outside the gate's execution context, which is precisely the
question the discarded evidence would have answered.

By contrast, a story that fails after dispatch retains per-story audit records,
per-iteration logs and captured agent output under the run directory. The
pre-dispatch baseline gate is the one failure that halts an entire sprint and it
produces the least recoverable record of any failure in the system.

## What was expected

Evidence that establishes why work was refused should outlive the refusal. A
check that halts a run before it begins is not a lesser event than a failure
occurring later in that run, and should retain what it observed at least as
durably — the observation that produced the verdict, not only a label naming
which check produced it, since a name identifies where to look while giving no
account of what was seen.

A workspace should not be reclaimed while it is still the only place a recorded
failure can be reproduced; cleanup of a transient environment belongs after
whatever evidence the run intends to keep has been captured out of it, not
before. Where evidence genuinely cannot be captured, the record should say that
it was unavailable, so that an absent account is distinguishable from an account
of nothing having gone wrong.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `991e2bd5ed378c8978049ebc58fb4449e9424db7` captured at `2026-08-04T02:54:00.036466+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `src/theforge/sprint/runner.py` — `sha256:7a4a3189156c984cadb13daa37f2719998bad4a663332df6f0687ea0149549e0`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/gate.py` — `sha256:459b3139b5a22ea02122c9c61023883977b53dd74b94fcc76069bbef1ff1c990`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/validate_phase.py` — `sha256:f20ce3ebcfb241f6c44f7d4e624da19e7c730ecfab7ec3e9c229ead6326b7d1c`
- `src/theforge/config/types.py` — `sha256:e20de0baa1579e94fb8a7cb57f402eebcd2fa8f2bdbcf164ba9c127b9eb3f3f0`
- `src/theforge/config/load.py` — `sha256:f455a4a3b92e672aa955707f125cd59eef4d7b3b5d86f91da32fdfd5182722eb`
- `src/theforge/traces.py` — `sha256:ab342a5be7630557265029241e5ea7d0b02060fb4ef82321585f7ceb3cc03e5e`
- `.forge/logs/issues-1415,2154,2155,2150/run-9c81cc51af26.log` — `sha256:b4f3fbe2cc4de8bf2bf3d224331ee572dbf17b5764b951ad27c2b83a75169214`

### Observed symptom

When the sprint baseline gate (the gate run against the sprint merge base
before any story is dispatched) fails, the run log ends up with only a
~2000-character tail of the gate's raw output (dominated by pytest's
trailing warnings-summary and short-summary lines), never the actual
assertion/traceback for the failing test — and the temporary git worktree
the gate ran in is deleted immediately afterward, in the same function call,
regardless of the gate's outcome. Both the durable record and the
reproducible environment are gone within the same call that produced the
failure, before any later investigation can happen.

### Reproduction / evidence

.forge/logs/issues-1415,2154,2155,2150/run-9c81cc51af26.log: the entire
record of the baseline gate failure is a `FAILED
tests/test_process_group.py::...` line plus a `1 failed, 6865 passed, ...`
pytest summary — no assertion text, no traceback. The worktree
`.forge/forge-baseline-hdkth9k6/worktree` no longer exists.

Code trace confirming the mechanism:
- src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:1225-1234 calls
  `run_gate_full(config, baseline_worktree, label=GateLabel(...))` for the
  baseline gate — no `task`, no `iter_num`, no `output_digest`.
- src/theforge/coordinator/gate.py:126-130: `write_trace(...)` (the
  mechanism that persists the gate's *full* raw output to
  `.forge/traces/<n>-gate.txt`) only runs `if iter_num is not None`. Since
  the baseline caller never passes `iter_num`, no full-output trace is ever
  written for the baseline gate — unlike per-story gate calls
  (src/theforge/coordinator/validate_phase.py:713-721), which pass
  `iter_num=state.dev_trace_count` and get a full trace file.
- src/theforge/coordinator/gate.py:135-136,150-151: on FAIL, only
  `output_tail = output[-tail_chars:]` (default 2000 chars,
  src/theforge/config/types.py:463) is logged, via
  `_cu._log(f"Gate command failed (exit non-zero): {output_tail}")`. This is
  the entire evidence that ends up in the run log — exactly the truncated
  tail observed (trailing warnings + summary line, no traceback, since
  pytest prints the FAILURES/traceback section well before the trailing
  warnings-summary and short-summary lines that fill the last 2000 chars).
- src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:1292-1300: the `finally:` block runs `git
  worktree remove --force` and `shutil.rmtree(temp_root, ...)`
  unconditionally — on PASS and FAIL alike — before `_run_baseline_gate`
  even returns to its caller, so nothing downstream (message logging,
  sprint-abort audit write at runner.py:3166-3191) has a chance to capture
  more from the workspace or preserve it for reproduction.
- Even the caller's own logging at runner.py:3165
  (`_log(str(baseline_gate.get("message", ...)))`) only emits the short
  `"Broken baseline: configured gate failed ..."` message string, which
  itself never includes `output_tail` (unlike
  `format_gate_failure_summary` in gate.py:155-180, which the baseline path
  does not use).

### Hypotheses tested

- **[ruled out]** The gate's full output was captured but simply never written to the run log by a logging bug
  - Evidence: gate.py:151 does log output_tail to the run log via _cu._log — the tail IS present in the log. The problem is upstream: only a 2000-char tail is ever computed (gate.py:135-136), and no full-output trace file is ever created for the baseline path because write_trace() is gated on iter_num being non-None (gate.py:126), which the baseline caller never supplies.
- **[ruled out]** The baseline worktree is deleted by some unrelated cleanup process (e.g. a later sprint-startup step or gc), not by _run_baseline_gate itself
  - Evidence: runner.py:1292-1300 shows the `finally:` block inside _run_baseline_gate itself removes the worktree and rmtrees temp_root unconditionally, immediately after run_gate_full returns, on both PASS and FAIL paths — there is no branch that skips cleanup or preserves the worktree on FAIL.
- **[confirmed]** Baseline gate evidence capture and worktree cleanup are structurally different from per-story gate handling, which does persist full output and (per gate.py's ESCALATE-worktree comment) can preserve worktrees on failure
  - Evidence: validate_phase.py:713-721 passes iter_num to run_gate_full, causing gate.py:126-130 to write a full-output trace file per story iteration. _run_baseline_gate (runner.py:1225-1234) never passes iter_num, so no equivalent trace exists for the baseline gate, and its finally block (runner.py:1292-1300) has no pass/fail branch analogous to the per-story ESCALATE-worktree preservation gate.py's docstring references (gate.py:170-172).

### Confirmed cause

`_run_baseline_gate` (src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:1077-1300) does two
things that together destroy the failure evidence:
(1) it calls `run_gate_full` without `iter_num` (runner.py:1225-1234), so
`write_trace`'s full-output persistence in
src/theforge/coordinator/gate.py:126-130 never fires for the baseline gate
— the only record of the failure is the bounded `output_tail` (last
`gate_output_tail_chars`, default 2000, chars of output), and
(2) its `finally:` block (runner.py:1292-1300) unconditionally removes the
temporary baseline worktree and rmtrees its parent temp dir on every path,
including FAIL, before the caller (runner.py:3161-3192) or anything else
gets a chance to capture more from it or preserve it for reproduction. The
combination means a baseline-gate FAIL leaves behind only a truncated
output tail (often just trailing pytest warnings/summary, not the actual
assertion/traceback) and no environment in which to reproduce or gather
more.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:1225-1234 (run_gate_full call site missing
iter_num), src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:1292-1300 (unconditional worktree
cleanup in the finally block), src/theforge/coordinator/gate.py:126-130
(write_trace gated on iter_num is not None).

### Fix-success criterion

When the sprint baseline gate fails, (a) a file under
`.forge/logs/<sprint-name>/` or equivalent persists the gate's full raw
output (or an explicit statement that it could not be captured), not just a
bounded tail, and this file/record survives past the end of the sprint run;
and (b) the temporary baseline worktree is not deleted until after that
evidence has been captured out of it — i.e. reproducing the failing test
against the preserved worktree/trace, or reading the persisted full output,
is possible after the sprint has already exited with "Broken baseline".

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- The named test (test_process_group.py::TestGroupMembers::test_lists_every_live_process_in_the_group) fails only inside the gate's baseline-worktree execution context and passes 34/34 when run directly against the same commit outside the gate — a separate environment-dependent flake worth its own investigation once evidence capture is fixed.

### Notes

This diagnosis explains why the specific reported failure
(test_process_group.py::TestGroupMembers::test_lists_every_live_process_in_the_group)
did not reproduce outside the gate three times — that is a distinct,
separate question (a possible test-isolation/environment-dependent flake in
that test) that this issue's evidence-preservation fix would make
answerable in the future but does not itself resolve. I did not attempt to
further diagnose why that specific test failed only inside the gate's
worktree/process context.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
